answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a time-delayed bond before it may earn reputation-weighted work. A violet audit committee randomly selects bonded agents to answer costly, verifiable tasks; failure or duplicate control evidence slashes the bond, while honest service gradually earns it back. A raven operator can still create many identities, but must lock capital per identity and risk losing it, so flooding an island of accounts becomes expensive rather than free.
